CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r4.speaker: Nöldeke
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r4.claim: Nöldeke cites al-Aʿshā Maimūn's verse praising someone as more generous with his benefits than a foaming Euphrates channel, supporting the sense benefit or gift.

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r5.claim: The Hebrew loan māʿūn apparently already meant benefit, gift, or donation in pre-Qur'anic Arabic.

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r6.speaker: Rhodokanakis
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r6.claim: Rhodokanakis agrees with Nöldeke and explains the Arabic semantic development through interference from maʿūna, from root ʿ-w-n.

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:7:anmerkung/r7.claim: A deliberate Qur'anic echo of Hebrew māʿôn remains possible despite the Arabic word's changed meaning.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r2.claim: The paired sūrahs al-Mā‘ūn and al-Kawthar portray Quraysh custodians as failed trustees who deserve removal, with the trust passing to worthy people.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r5.claim: Because they are misers, the custodians will not spend for God's sake or even lend small items of common use.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r7.claim: Its custodians were charged with these tasks, but the unworthy leaders cannot fulfil them, so the following sūrah settles their fate.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r5.claim: The two closing verses identify ostentation and miserliness as the causes of impure, devotionless prayer.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p473/r8.claim: Miserliness proves prayer is lifeless: gratitude to God should make a person generous and recognize the needy's rightful claim in one's wealth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r1.claim: Prayer is the foremost expression of gratitude and leads a person to spend for God's sake; prayer and spending are the two pillars of the sharī‘ah.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r2.claim: Mā‘ūn means items of common use.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r3.claim: Borrowing and lending common items is normal among neighbours and supports a healthy social structure and bonds of friendship and fraternity.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r4.claim: A decent person should readily help a neighbour with ordinary needs; only mean people refuse such help.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p474/r5.claim: Mean people pray to impress others, without inner motivation or effect on their hearts; ostentation increases their callousness.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r1.claim: After condemning failure in one's duties toward people, the surah criticizes those who fail to fulfill genuine duties of worship toward God.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r11.claim: The surah stresses that sincere worship of God and mutual aid and solidarity cannot be separated in religious devotion.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r12.claim: A truly believing person fulfills duties toward God and creation sincerely, does good, and enables rather than blocks its spread through social cooperation.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r2.claim: Three faults are given among people who pray: distance from prayer's essence, ostentation in worship, and obstructing good.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r6.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r6.claim: Tabari reports that ma'un has been explained as alms, other financial duties, benefits people withhold from each other, a right, a loan, or property.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r7.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:4/r7.claim: Tabari understands ma'un broadly as kindness, good, and sharing benefits; the authors likewise render it with the broad word “good.”

STUDYQURAN:107:7/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r1.claim: The verse describes people who perform devotions well but fail to act kindly toward others.

STUDYQURAN:107:7/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r2.speaker: widespread interpretation
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r2.claim: Māʿūn commonly means utensils or tools that neighbors share or lend, such as a pickax, pot, or bucket.

STUDYQURAN:107:7/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r3.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r3.claim: Other interpretations take māʿūn as anything beneficial, obligatory zakāh, property generally in Qurayshi dialect, or refusing guests.

STUDYQURAN:107:7/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:7/r4.claim: All readings point to hypocrites' stinginess: they attend prayer lazily and spend reluctantly.

STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.claim: Most call al-Māʿūn an early Makkan sūrah after al-Takāthur, though some assign vv. 4–7 to Madinah; since the whole sūrah addresses religious hypocrisy, it may all be Madinan, when hypocrisy could gain political advantage.

STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.claim: Religious hypocrisy is not treated as limited to Muslims alone.

STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r3.claim: The sūrah takes its name from māʿūn in its last verse, broadly meaning kindness, charity, or assistance.
